Title: Building a custom machine out of Lego bricks

When building a custom machine out of Lego bricks, you first need to develop the basic design.
After that, you order certain Lego brick sets.
You give the lego sets to a group of children which should sort the parts for you (into a number of containers).
Your machine is built out of a number of subcomponents.
You build them individually, using parts from the sorted containers.
If there are no more parts in a container, you reorder individual parts.
After building each subcomponent, you have to test them individually and (if each test is successful) assemble them.
If subcomponents are not tested successfully, you have to redesign and rebuild them.

If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.

result.rule: When The description says that each produced part must be verified by its own check before a later step, and that a failed check requires rework of that part before the process can continue.: Model each verification as its own activity after the production activity it checks. Follow it with an exclusive gateway whose outgoing flows carry the success condition (continuing to the next step) and the failure condition (returning to the rework activity). Do not fold the verification into the production activity or omit the decision.

When the description says several activities are performed independently of each other and all of them must be completed before a later step can begin: Model a parallel gateway that splits the flow into one branch per independent activity, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches so the later step starts only after all of them finish. Do not leave the branches unsynchronized, and do not use an exclusive gateway for a join that requires every branch.

When the description lists two or more actions that must each be carried out, such as notifying different parties, without stating an order between them, and the process continues only after all of them are done: Model each such action as its own branch that starts from a parallel gateway, and join the branches with a parallel gateway before the next step. Do not use an exclusive gateway, and do not add conditions to these branches.

When the description states that two or more activities or branches may run at the same time with no required order, and a later step is described as starting only after all of them are finished (or as needing their results); a branch may also state that some of its work must be repeated a minimum number of times: Open the concurrent branches with a parallel gateway, with one outgoing flow per branch, and close them with a parallel gateway (join) before the dependent step, so the later step waits for all branches. If a branch must repeat its work a stated minimum number of times, model that work as a task inside a loop: an exclusive gateway after the task returns the flow to the task until the minimum count is reached, then passes it on. Add no conditions to the fork or join flows, and do not replace the join with an exclusive gateway.
